en: Dhātukathā 2 Niddesa 2.9. Exposition of the Ninth Method:
The State of Being Associated with that which is Not Associated (Sampayuttena-asampayutta-pada-niddesa)
Those phenomena associated with the aggregate of feeling (vedanākkhandha),
those phenomena associated with the aggregate of perception (saññākkhandha),

and those phenomena associated with the aggregate of mental formations (saṅkhārakkhandha)— with those phenomena, how many aggregates, how many bases, and how many elements are the [associated] phenomena associated?
Those states are associated with three aggregates, one base, and seven elements;
they are associated with one base and one element by some [factors].
Those states which [are associated] with the consciousness aggregate...
Those phenomena associated with the mind-base … those phenomena associated with the eye-consciousness-element … [and so on] … those phenomena associated with the mind-element …

Those phenomena associated with the mental-consciousness element (manoviññāṇadhātu), and those phenomena associated with those [mental] phenomena … [and so on] … those phenomena are associated with three aggregates (khandha);
they are associated with one base (āyatana) and one element (dhātu) by way of some [of their factors].
Those phenomena associated with the truth of the origin,
and those phenomena associated with the truth of the path—
those phenomena which are associated with these [latter] phenomena are associated with three aggregates, one base, and one element.
They are associated with one aggregate, one base, and one element, and with certain [other] factors.
Those factors which are associated with the mind-faculty (manindriya), and those factors which are associated with those [same] factors—
those factors are associated with three aggregates.
They are associated with one base and one element by some [factors].
Those phenomena that are associated with the faculty of pleasure … those phenomena that are associated with the faculty of pain …
Those phenomena associated with the faculty of mental joy (*somanassindriya*),
and those phenomena associated with the faculty of mental grief (*domanassindriya*), and those phenomena associated with those [former] phenomena—
those phenomena are associated with three aggregates (*khandha*), one base (*āyatana*), and one element (*dhātu*).
They are associated with one base (āyatana) and one element (dhātu),
and with certain [mental] factors. Those factors which are associated with the equanimity faculty (upekkhindriya)—
those factors which are associated with those [former] factors… those factors are associated with three aggregates (khandha), one base, and six elements.
They are associated with one base (āyatana) and one element (dhātu),
and with certain [mental] factors. Those phenomena that are associated with the faculty of faith (saddhindriya)… those phenomena that are associated with the faculty of energy (vīriyindriya)…
Those phenomena by means of the faculty of mindfulness … those phenomena by means of the faculty of concentration … those phenomena by means of the faculty of wisdom …
Those phenomena [associated] with the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown," those phenomena [associated] with the faculty of final knowledge,
and those phenomena [associated] with the faculty of one who has already known.
Those states which are associated with ignorance... those states which are associated with the volitional formations conditioned by ignorance...
those states which are associated with those states [are] associated with three aggregates, one base, and one element.
They are associated with one aggregate (khandha), one base (āyatana), and one element (dhātu).

Those phenomena which are associated with consciousness (viññāṇa) through the condition of volitional formations (saṅkhāra-paccaya)— those phenomena which are associated with those [consciousness] phenomena—
are themselves associated with three aggregates.
They are associated with one base (āyatana) and one element (dhātu), and with certain [factors] that are associated.
Those factors which are associated with contact (phassa) by way of the condition of the six bases (saḷāyatana-paccaya)—those factors which are associated with those factors [are as follows]:
those factors are associated with three aggregates (khandha), one base, and seven elements.
They are associated with one aggregate, one base, and one element, and with certain [other] factors.
Those factors which are associated with feeling by way of the condition of contact, and those factors which are associated with those factors...
those factors are associated with three aggregates, one base, and seven elements.
They are associated with one base and one element by way of some [mental factors].
Those phenomena that arise with feeling as condition for craving;
those phenomena that arise with craving as condition for clinging...
Those phenomena that are associated with the kamma-existence, and those phenomena that are associated with those [former] phenomena:
these phenomena are associated with three aggregates, one base, and one element;
they are associated with some [phenomena] by way of one aggregate, one base, and one element.
Those phenomena associated with ignorance...
those phenomena associated with suffering...
those phenomena associated with mental distress; and those phenomena associated with those [aforementioned] phenomena...
Those states are associated with three aggregates, one base, and one element;
they are associated with one base and one element by some [of them].
Those states which [are associated] with despair...
Those phenomena associated with the foundations of mindfulness,
those phenomena associated with the right exertions, and those phenomena associated with those [latter] phenomena—
those phenomena are associated with three aggregates, one base, and one element.
They are associated with one aggregate, one base, and one element, and with certain [factors].
Those factors which are associated with the bases of psychic power (iddhipāda)—those factors which are associated with those factors [are as follows]:
those factors are associated with two aggregates.
They are associated with one base (āyatana) and one element (dhātu), and with certain [mental] factors.
Those factors which are associated with the jhāna—those factors which are associated with those factors [are as follows]:
those factors are associated with two aggregates (khandha), one base, and one element.
They are associated with one aggregate (khandha), one base (āyatana), and one element (dhātu).
As for those phenomena associated with the immeasurables (appamaññā) … as for those phenomena associated with the five faculties (indriya) …
Those phenomena that are associated with the five powers;
those phenomena that are associated with the seven factors of enlightenment;
those phenomena that are associated with the noble eightfold path; and those phenomena that are associated with those [aforementioned] phenomena.
Those states are associated with three aggregates, one base, and one element;
they are associated with some [states] through one aggregate, one base, and one element.
Those states which [are associated] with contact...
Those phenomena which are associated with volition… those phenomena which are associated with attention, and those phenomena which are associated with those [latter] phenomena—
those phenomena are associated with three aggregates, one base, and seven elements.
They are associated with one aggregate, one base, and one element, and with certain [other] factors.
Those factors which are associated with feeling...
those factors which are associated with perception... those factors which are associated with those factors...
Those states are associated with three aggregates, one base, and seven elements;
they are associated with one base and one element by some [factors].
Those states which are associated with consciousness—those states which are associated with those states...
Those states are associated with three aggregates;
they are associated with one base and one element by some [of their factors].
Those states which are associated with resolve—those states which are associated with those states...
Those states are associated with three aggregates, one base, and two elements;
they are associated with one aggregate, one base, and one element by some [factors].
2.9.1. Triads.
Those phenomena which are associated with phenomena associated with pleasant feeling;
those phenomena which are associated with phenomena associated with painful feeling;
those phenomena which are associated with phenomena associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling; and those phenomena which are associated with those [latter] phenomena.
Those states are associated with one aggregate;
they are associated with one base and one element by some [factors].
As for those states that are associated with states having applied thought and sustained thought...
Those phenomena which are associated with phenomena that possess only investigation and sustained thought;
those phenomena which are associated with phenomena accompanied by rapture;
those phenomena which are associated with those [latter] phenomena—they are associated with one aggregate, one base, and one element.
Those states which are associated with states accompanied by pleasure...
those states which are associated with states accompanied by equanimity, and those states which are associated with those [latter] states...
those states are associated with one aggregate.
Associated with one base and with one element by some [factors].
The Group on Roots (Hetugocchaka).
Those phenomena which are associated with phenomena that are roots;
those phenomena which are associated with phenomena that are both roots and accompanied by roots;
those phenomena which are associated with phenomena that are both roots and associated with roots; and those phenomena which are associated with those [latter] phenomena.
Those states are associated with three aggregates, one base, and one element;
they are associated with some [states] by means of one aggregate, one base, and one element.
Those states which, together with those states that have causes but are not themselves causes...
Those phenomena which are associated with phenomena that are both root-possessing and not themselves roots;
those phenomena which are associated with phenomena that are neither roots nor root-possessing;
those phenomena which are associated with those [latter] phenomena—those phenomena are associated with one aggregate, one base, and one element, and with certain others.
2.9.2.3. The Group on Taints (Āsavagocchaka).
Those phenomena which [are associated] with the taints;
those phenomena which [are associated] with both the taints and the tainted.
Those states which are associated with the taints (*āsava*) and with states associated with the taints, and those states which are associated with those states...
those states are associated with three aggregates (*khandha*), one base (*āyatana*), and one element (*dhātu*);
[or] they are associated with one aggregate, one base, and one element, and with some [others].
Those states which are associated with states that are both associated with the taints (*āsava*) and not themselves taints, and which are further associated with those [latter] states:
those states are associated with one aggregate (*khandha*), one base (*āyatana*), and one element (*dhātu*), and with certain others.
2.9.2.4–9. The Group on Fetters (*saṃyojana-gocchaka*), etc.
Those states which are associated with the fetters … with the ties … with the floods … with the yokes … with the hindrances … with the misapprehensions;
those states which are associated with both the misapprehensions and the states that are objects of misapprehension;
those states which are associated with those [latter] states—those states are associated with three aggregates, one base, and one element.
They are associated with one aggregate, one base, and one element, and with some [factors].
Those factors which are associated with the factors associated with the perversions (parāmāsa), and those factors which are associated with those factors...
those factors are associated with one aggregate, one base, and one element, and with some [factors].
2.9.2.10. Mahantaraduka:
Those phenomena which are associated with states that are themselves associated with consciousness—those phenomena are associated with three aggregates.
They are associated with one base and with one element by way of some [mental factors].
Those phenomena which [are associated] with mental factors … those phenomena which [are associated] with mind-associates …
Those phenomena which [arise] through phenomena associated with consciousness;
those phenomena which [arise] through phenomena associated with and originated by consciousness;
those phenomena which [arise] through phenomena associated with, originated by, and co-existent with consciousness.
Those phenomena which are associated with those phenomena that are conjoined with, originated by, and follow upon the mind; and those phenomena which are associated with those [first] phenomena ...
those phenomena are associated with one aggregate (khandha), one base (āyatana), and seven elements (dhātu).
2.9.2.11–13. The Group on Grasping (Upādāna-gocchaka), etc.
Those phenomena which [arise] from phenomena that are objects of clinging;
those phenomena which [arise] from phenomena that are defilements;
those phenomena which [arise] from phenomena that are both defilements and subject to defilement.
Those phenomena which are associated with both the defilements and the defiled phenomena;
those phenomena which are associated with both the defilements and the phenomena associated with the defilements;
those phenomena which are associated with those [latter] phenomena—these phenomena are associated with three aggregates, one base, and one element.
They are associated with one aggregate, one base, and one element by way of certain [factors].
As for those factors which are associated with defiled states but are not themselves defilements...
as for those factors which are associated with states that are associated with defilements but are not themselves defilements...
Those phenomena which [arise] with phenomena accompanied by applied thought...
those phenomena which [arise] with phenomena accompanied by sustained thought...
those phenomena which [arise] with phenomena accompanied by rapture...
Those phenomena which are associated with phenomena accompanied by rapture (*pītisahagata*), and those phenomena which are associated with those [first] phenomena—
those phenomena are associated with one aggregate (*khandha*), one base (*āyatana*), and one element (*dhātu*).
Those phenomena which are associated with phenomena accompanied by pleasure (*sukhasahagata*)...

Regarding those phenomena associated with states accompanied by equanimity, and those phenomena associated with those [first] phenomena—how many aggregates, how many bases, and how many elements are those phenomena associated with?
Those phenomena are associated with one aggregate;
they are associated with some with one base and one element.
The four formless aggregates,
the mind base itself,
and the seven consciousness elements.
There are two truths and fourteen faculties.
In the section on conditions there are twelve terms,
and beyond that, sixteen.
In the *Tika* there are eight groups,
and in the *Mahantaraduka* there are seven, making forty-three altogether.
In the pairs, there are six footings;
these have been included in the exposition of the ninth footing. [120]
The ninth [chapter], the exposition of the associated state by way of what is associated with it.
